examples: The elaborate cake had many layers.

more.def: Made carefully with many parts and details.
examples: The elaborate cake had five layers.
She wore an elaborate costume to the party.
The plan was too elaborate to follow.

more.def: To pass by, as time does.
examples: An hour elapsed before the bus came.
Several years elapsed before they met again.
Time elapsed quickly during the game.

easy.def: Able to stretch and spring back.

more.def: Able to stretch and then go back to its shape.
examples: A rubber band is elastic, so it snaps back when you let go.
The elastic waist of the pants is comfortable.
Elastic cloth is used to make socks.
Mom sewed elastic in my pants.

more.def: A stretchy cord or cloth used in clothes to hold them in place.
examples: Mom sewed elastic into the waist of my skirt.
The elastic in my sock wore out.
A piece of elastic held the mask on.

more.def: Extremely happy and excited.
examples: She was elated when she won the prize.
He felt elated after scoring the goal.
There was elation at the win.

more.def: A feeling of great joy and excitement.
examples: She jumped up and down in elation when she won.
There was elation in the crowd.
He felt elation after crossing the finish line.

easy.def: The part in the middle of your arm that bends.

more.def: The joint in the middle of your arm where it bends.
examples: I bumped my elbow on the door.
She rested her elbows on the table.
He bent his elbow and flexed his muscle.

more.def: Older than another person, usually in the same family.
examples: My elder sister is in fifth grade.
The elder of the two brothers cooked dinner.
She looked after her elder cousin's dog.

easy.def: An older person who is respected.

more.def: An older person who is respected by a group.
examples: The village elders told stories by the fire.
The tribe's elders met to settle the dispute.
The elders gave advice to the young.

more.def: A small, dark purple fruit that grows on a bush and is used for jam.
examples: We picked elderberries to make jam.
Elderberry syrup is dark and sweet.
An elderly man crossed the street.

more.def: Quite old; a polite way to say that a person is in the later part of life.
examples: An elderly man sat on the bench in the sun.
We helped our elderly neighbor carry her groceries.
The elderly woman told us stories about her childhood.

more.def: To choose someone for a job by voting.
examples: The town elected a new mayor.
We voted to elect her captain.

easy.def: A time when people vote to choose a leader.
examples: Our class had an election for president.

more.def: A time when people vote to choose a leader or decide something.
examples: The class held an election for president.
The election is held every four years.
Many people waited in line to vote on election day.

more.def: Using or run by electricity.
examples: The electric train ran along the track.

more.def: Having to do with electricity or using it.
examples: An electrical wire runs through the wall.
The electrician checked the electrical outlet.
The toy needs an electrical cord.

easy.def: A person who fixes and puts in wires for electricity.

more.def: A person whose job is to install and repair electric wires and equipment in buildings.
examples: The electrician fixed the broken light switch in the kitchen.
We called an electrician to put in new wires.
The electrician wore rubber gloves to stay safe.

easy.def: A kind of power that runs lights and machines.
examples: The storm knocked out the electricity.

more.def: A form of energy that flows through wires and makes lights and machines work.
examples: The storm knocked out the electricity in our town.
Wires carry electricity to our homes.
Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.

more.def: To supply with electric power, or to thrill.
examples: They electrified the village with new wires.
The railroad was electrified last year.

easy.def: About electricity and a pull like magnets have.

more.def: About both electricity and magnetism.
examples: Light is a kind of electromagnetic wave.

easy.def: A tiny bit of an atom that carries electricity.

more.def: A tiny part of an atom that has a negative electric charge.
examples: Electrons move around the center of an atom.
Electricity is the flow of electrons through a wire.
An electron is much smaller than an atom.

more.def: Using tiny parts that control electricity, such as in computers and phones.
examples: The electronic game beeped and flashed.

easy.def: Machines like phones and TVs that use electricity.

more.def: Machines and devices that use tiny electric parts to work, such as phones, computers and televisions.
examples: The store sells electronics such as televisions, tablets and speakers.
Please turn off all electronics during the test.
Tiny parts inside electronics send signals very quickly.

more.def: Beauty and good taste in the way something looks or moves.
examples: The ballerina moved across the stage with elegance.
The simple room had a quiet elegance.
She walked with elegance in her long gown.

more.def: Graceful, stylish and pleasing to look at.
examples: She wore an elegant gown to the ball.
The swan moved with elegant grace.
The room was simple and elegant.
Water is one element of a lake.
The story has an element of surprise.

more.def: A basic part of something larger, or a simple substance such as gold or oxygen.
examples: Gold is an element found in the ground.
Oxygen is an element in the air we breathe.
Fire needs three elements: fuel, heat and air.

more.def: Basic, simple and natural, like the forces of fire, water, earth and air.
examples: Food and water are elemental needs.
The storm showed the elemental power of nature.

more.def: Simple and basic; dealing with the first or easiest part of something.
examples: We learned elementary facts about plants in science class.
Counting to ten is an elementary skill for young children.
The elementary rules of the game are easy to learn.

easy.def: A very big gray animal with a long trunk.

more.def: The largest animal that lives on land, with a long trunk and big ears.
examples: The elephant sprayed water with its trunk.
An elephant can weigh thousands of pounds.
The baby elephant followed its mother.
The crane will elevate the beam.

more.def: To raise something to a higher place, or to make something better.
examples: The nurse told him to elevate his sore foot.
The crane elevated the beam to the top of the building.
Good music can elevate your mood.

easy.def: How high a place is above the sea.
examples: The town is at a high elevation.
The elevation of the hill is tall.

more.def: The height of a place above the level of the sea.
examples: The town sits at an elevation of five thousand feet.
At high elevation, the air is thin and cool.
The map shows the elevation of each hill.

easy.def: A small room that moves people up and down in a building.
examples: We took the elevator to the top floor.
Push the button for the elevator.

more.def: A small moving room that carries people from one floor of a building to another.
examples: The elevator stopped at the fifth floor.
An elevator carried the luggage to the hotel rooms.
Please use the elevator if you have heavy bags.
There are eleven players on a soccer team.

more.def: The number that comes after ten, written 11.
examples: A soccer team puts eleven players on the field.
My brother is eleven years old.

more.def: Coming after the tenth one and before the twelfth.
examples: She celebrated her eleventh birthday at the park.
He finished eleventh in the race.
The eleventh player on the team scored the goal.

easy.def: A tiny person in stories with pointy ears.
examples: An elf lives in the woods.

more.def: A small, magical person in stories who often has pointed ears.
examples: The elf in the story made shoes at night.
An elf with pointy ears appeared.

easy.def: Small and light, like a make-believe elf.

more.def: Small, delicate and playful, like an elf.
examples: The girl had an elfin face with pointed ears.
The dancer was small and elfin.

easy.def: Allowed to do something because you fit the rules.
examples: She is eligible for the race.
He is eligible for a prize.

more.def: Having the right to take part in something because you meet the rules.
examples: Anyone over eighteen is eligible to vote.
She is eligible for the race because she is ten.
Only students in the third grade are eligible for the prize.

more.def: To remove something completely, or to knock a player out of a contest.
examples: We want to eliminate waste at school.
Our team was eliminated in the first round.
Washing your hands eliminates many germs.
She is in the elite group.

more.def: Being the best or most skilled of a group.
examples: The elite swimmers trained every day.
She joined an elite team of climbers.
Only elite players are chosen for that team.

more.def: A magical liquid in stories that is said to cure sickness or give a person long life.
examples: In the fairy tale, the wizard mixed an elixir that would make you young again.
The hero drank the elixir and felt strong at once.
The old woman sold bottles of elixir at the market.

easy.def: A very big wild animal like a deer.

more.def: A very large deer that lives in North America, the male having wide antlers.
examples: We saw an elk in the park.
Elk gather in herds in the valley.

more.def: Shaped like a stretched circle; oval.
examples: The planet moves in an elliptical orbit.

more.def: A large tree with a wide top and rough leaves that gives plenty of shade.
examples: We sat in the shade of a huge elm.
The elm tree lined the old street.
Elm leaves turn yellow in the fall.

more.def: To make something longer or to become longer.
examples: Shadows elongate in the late afternoon.
She elongated the dress by adding a ruffle.
The clay elongated as he pulled it.

more.def: Fluent, beautiful and powerful speaking or writing.
Able to speak in a clear, beautiful and powerful way.
examples: The eloquent speaker moved the crowd.

more.def: In addition, or different from what has been named.
examples: Is there anything else you need for your project?
If the park is closed, where else can we play?
Ask someone else if you cannot find me.
If it is not here, look elsewhere.

more.def: In or to a different place.
examples: He moved elsewhere to find work.
The rain fell elsewhere, but not here.

easy.def: To escape from someone by being clever.

more.def: To escape from someone or something, or to be hard to understand or remember.
examples: The rabbit eluded the fox by darting into a hole.
The answer to the riddle eluded him.
Sleep eluded her the night before the trip.

more.def: Hard to find, catch or remember.
examples: The elusive fox slipped away into the trees.
The answer to the riddle was elusive.
The rare bird was elusive and hard to spot.
